description: Registry binding designmd's HTML/CSS classes to the two systems they answer to: Picasso (github.com/toptal/picasso — the source of truth, React + Storybook) and the Figma component library. Each entry carries the designmd side (root class, snippet, shortcode), a react block (component, import, storyId, propMap, status) verified against Picasso's source, and a figma block. designmd is an extension of Picasso, not a parallel system: where a token or prop differs, Picasso is right.

figmaLibrary.name: Product Library v2.0
figmaLibrary.status: discovered — 214 published components; matched below. propMaps + Code Connect templates pending (phase 2).

conventions.designmd.root: Primary CSS class (or attribute) that identifies the component in HTML.
conventions.designmd.snippet: Canonical minimal markup — what Claude emits when building the feature in HTML/CSS.
conventions.figma.component: Exact Figma component / component-set name in the published library.
conventions.figma.propMap: Maps Figma variant/property values -> designmd variant classes, e.g. {"Variant":{"Primary":"btn-primary"}}.
conventions.react.block: Cross-reference to the React/Storybook library (Picasso). Fields: component, import, storyId, status, propMap, note.
conventions.react.status: mapped = clean 1:1 · partial = closest fit, see note · gap = no single Picasso component (compose).
conventions.slug: Stable key stamped as data-component="<slug>"; the ?map=1 inspector resolves it to this entry.
conventions.stampSelector: CSS selector the inspector uses to auto-stamp data-component; omit to register without auto-stamping.
conventions.react.propMap: designmd class -> Picasso props. Key order is precedence: the root class comes first and modifiers after, so the result does not depend on the order a prototype writes its classes. Keys that are not classes (e.g. tooltip's "data-placement=top") document the binding but are not resolved by the ?map=1 inspector, which matches on classList.

react.note: Icon is chosen by name, not by a variant prop, so there is nothing to propMap. SIZING MATCHES EXACTLY: designmd's .icon is width/height 1em with vertical-align -0.125em, and Picasso's icon components carry h-[1em] align-[-.125em]. COLOUR DIFFERS IN APPROACH: Picasso uses fill-current + text-inherit, so every icon inherits its parent's colour; designmd uses fill:none + color: var(--color-icon) and overrides to inherit inside colour-carrying contexts (.btn, a, .badge, .tag, .toast). Same result in those contexts, but a standalone designmd icon rests at graphite-750 where Picasso's would take the surrounding text colour. NAMES: 231 of designmd's 325 sprite slugs match one of Picasso's 311 icons exactly (71%). 87 are genuinely designmd-only and 80 Picasso-only. Seven more look like the same icon under a different name and are worth reconciling: controls/control, cpu/cpu2, cpu-2/cpu2, flag-2/flag2, initiatives/initiative, performance-2/performance, play/player. Note Picasso ships Ach and CreditCard at 32 as well as 16/24, so 'two grids' is true of designmd's pack but not strictly of Picasso's.

Picasso resolves variant x size into a size class, a weight AND a colour. The nine plain roles map exactly; the five -semibold ones need weight passed because Picasso's body variant is always font-regular. COLOUR DIVERGES: Picasso sets headings text-black and body text-graphite-700, while designmd gives everything --color-text (graphite-900), so prototype body copy reads darker than the product's. .caption resolves identically to .body-xs. --type-mono has no Picasso equivalent. Picasso's heading/xsmall — text-md at regular weight — has no designmd counterpart.
